subject: swampTroll
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: swamp troll with tusks, mohawk and bone fetishes.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.
reasoning:
I'm planning the design for a hunched Warcraft-style swamp troll with tusks, a mohawk, bone fetishes, and a loincloth, and starting to lay out the skeletal structure for the model.

Building the spine and neck chains...

For color, I'm going with mottled green troll skin with a pale belly and countershading. For the head, I'm sculpting a skull with a brow ridge, a prominent troll nose, tusks on the jaw, and small yellow eyes with dark pupils.

Still working out the mohawk blades and ear shapes...

Now I'm setting up the leg structure: hips positioned symmetrically, feet targets below, with two-segment IK chains for each leg and checking the reach distance fits within the limb lengths before naming the joint chains.

Still placing leg and foot geometry...

For arms, I'm positioning shoulders, elbows, and wrists in a resting extended pose, angling elbows outward and down toward the wrists.

Defining finger chains...

Working out hit-testing with surface rays instead—casting from front at varying heights to find the actual body surface, then positioning the pendant string along a sagging U-curve between those hit points.

I'm adding small skulls and bone cylinders alternating along the string, plus feather tufts and a larger central skull fetish piece. For the loincloth, I'm considering extruding a flat cloth shape at the hips with a tribal pattern texture, positioned in front using thin-extrude geometry rather than a flat plane.

I'm also figuring out the belt as a swept ring around the hips using a surface loop, adjusting the anchor height to avoid missing the body mesh since the sweep starts lower than the hips joint.

Then I'm adding hanging bone fetishes along the belt loop, placing small cylinder bones that point downward from offset positions around the ring, bound to the hips bone.

For shoulder and back details, I'm adding tusk spikes on a shoulder pad and a hunched sphere bump on the upper back. For the head, I'm defining the head's local frame with forward/up/right directions, then placing a skull using a sphere scaled unevenly along world axes and positioned slightly forward and up from the head joint.

Continuing the facial features, I'm sketching out a wide brow box, a hooked nose made from a scaled sphere with nostrils, and a lower jaw bone built from another scaled sphere offset down and forward to create an underbite, plus an upper jaw/muzzle sphere positioned just above it.

Now I'm working on the tusks, sweeping curved bezier shapes outward from the jaw corners with pointed caps, figuring out how to position them symmetrically left and right using the head's local coordinate system.

I'll write a helper that converts signed x-values into left/right local offsets for the head frame, then use it to place glowing yellow-orange eyes with dark sockets, and start outlining pointed ears extruding from the sides of the head.

Now I'm defining the ear outline as a shaped silhouette with sharp tips, mirrored for both sides with thickness along the z-axis, then moving on to the mohawk blades positioned in a row from forehead to back of the neck.

Adding spiky spines along the back and shoulders using downward raycasts to place cones on the surface, then I'm setting up the skin paint with a mottled green countershade and starting a custom moss-coloring function based on surface normals.

For feet, I'm gradienting the skin color into a muddy brown near the ground to suggest legs caked in dirt. I'm also planning a tribal tattoo decal placed on the chest using a directional projection.

Now I'm adding feather details hanging from a belt and shoulder pad using card frames, giving three total textures (rune, tattoo, feather). I'm skipping tails and moving into writing the actual bone/pendant code using a stick-bone helper that embeds objects onto hit points.

Adding hanging bone and skull pendants...

Adding spikes scattered across the pad, then building the hand with a palm sphere at the wrist and three tapered fingers as small polyline chains parented to the arm tip.

Still writing creature parts...

Adding a chest tattoo decal by raycasting forward from the chest point, then sketching a feather SVG with a teal/red spine shape. I'm also placing card frames and belt feathers using the along-path helper to distribute frames around the loop.

Now I'm working out the belt sweep around the body surface, adding a skull buckle, and figuring out the loincloth placement relative to the body's front z-position at belt height.

For the cloth itself, I'm shaping a hip-hung outline that tapers from wide at the top to a sharp point at the bottom, attached at the belt line with proper thickness and bone weighting. Then I'm placing a decorative rune plane flush against the cloth's front face, sized and positioned to sit centered over it.

Now moving to texturing: glow only applies to the eyes, while the mohawk gets a gradient paint blending red to orange based on height along the strip. Tusks are built from curved control points rising up beside the muzzle, starting at the jaw and sweeping outward and upward.

I'm also sketching small jaw teeth as tiny cones, placing toe positions on the feet, and checking overall height comes to about 2.6 units including the mohawk, which fits the hunched troll proportions. Then I lay out the spine chain with three joints along a sweeping body path, and define the neck as a short polyline connecting the upper spine to the base of the head.

Now I'm finishing the neck chain parented to the spine's last joint, sizing its taper radii, and positioning the head joint at the neck's end with a slight forward offset so the skull sits naturally over the chest, keeping the heavy hunched posture consistent. Time to write it all out.
